title: Julieta Ramírez Villazana
text: I am a graduate student in Economics at The University of Texas at El Paso, specializing in econometrics and time series analysis. My research interests lie at the intersection of economic history and labor economics, particularly the economics of women’s work, both paid professional labor and unpaid or unrecognized work.

title: Julieta Ramírez Villazana
text:
Research Project
Structural Breaks in U.S. Women’s Labor Force Participation by Age Group ECON 5371, Time Series Analysis and Forecasting (Fall 2026)
When did women’s labor force participation change course, and did it happen at the same time for every generation? This project tests for structural breaks in the participation rates of seven age groups, using annual Current Population Survey data from 1948 to 2025, and links each break to its historical and policy context.

Data: U.S. Department of Labor, Women’s Bureau (BLS Current Population Survey)
Methods: structural break tests with known and unknown break dates
Tools: Python (pandas, statsmodels)
Status: paper in progress; results and dashboard coming December 2026

https://rmzjulieta.github.io/econ5371/ · Paper (coming soon) · Dashboard (coming soon)
